title: The password that found Portugal
scenario: A software company runs semantic search over its help centre. In March, a job embedded every help article. In September, the team upgraded the query service to a newer Gemini embedding model and left the stored vectors alone. Since then, users get strange results. You review the setup and one search (exhibit).
exhibit:
INDEX JOB (ran 2026-03-02)
  model:   gemini-embedding-001
  input:   raw article text, no prefix
  stored:  18,400 vectors, 3072 dims each

QUERY SERVICE (deployed 2026-09-28)
  model:   gemini-embedding-2
  input:   "task: search result | query: " + user_question

SEARCH LOG 2026-10-01
  query:   how do I reset my password?
  top hit: "Shipping times for Portugal"
  article that should match: "Reset your password"

questions.prompt: Why does the password question return a shipping article?

options.text: The query prefix is in the wrong format for a search task.
options.explanation: The prefix matches the format the Gemini docs give for a search query: `task: search result | query:` followed by the text.

options.text: Help articles are too long to embed, so most of their text was cut.
options.explanation: Length is not what changed in September. The search broke when the query model changed while the stored vectors stayed the same.

options.text: Queries and articles were embedded by two models with incompatible spaces.
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini docs say embeddings from `gemini-embedding-001` and `gemini-embedding-2` cannot be directly compared.

options.text: Semantic search cannot match questions to answers that use other words than the question.
options.explanation: It can. That is its main strength: in the OpenAI retrieval guide, the best answer to a moon question shares no words with it.

questions.prompt: The team wants to keep `gemini-embedding-2`. What must they do with the 18,400 stored vectors?

options.explanation: Right. The Gemini docs: if you are upgrading to `gemini-embedding-2`, you must re-embed all of your existing data.

options.text: Normalize the stored vectors to length 1 so they line up with the new ones.
options.explanation: Normalizing changes a vector's length, not the space it lives in. Vectors from the two models still cannot be compared.

options.text: Cut the stored vectors down to 768 numbers, one of the recommended sizes.
options.explanation: Size is not the problem: the default output size for both models is 3072. The old vectors come from a different space at any size.

options.text: Add the same task prefix to the stored vectors as the query service uses.
options.explanation: A prefix goes into the text before embedding. It cannot be added to vectors that already exist, so the articles must be embedded again.

questions.prompt: When they re-embed, how should each help article's text be formatted for `gemini-embedding-2`?

options.text: `task: search result | query: ` followed by the article text.
options.explanation: That is the query structure. In the asymmetric search case, the Gemini docs give a different structure for documents.

options.text: The raw article text, with `task_type` set to `RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT`.
options.explanation: `task_type` is for `gemini-embedding-001`. The Gemini docs say you cannot use the `task_type` field with `gemini-embedding-2`.

options.text: The raw article text with no prefix, as in the March job.
options.explanation: For text-only tasks with `gemini-embedding-2`, the Gemini docs strongly recommend adding the task format, so plain text ignores that advice.

options.text: `title: ` and the article title, then ` | text: ` and the body.
options.explanation: Right. For search, question answering and similar asymmetric tasks, the Gemini docs give the document structure `title: {title} | text: {content}`.

questions.prompt: Their new vector database stores at most 1,024 numbers per vector. What fits the Gemini docs best?

options.text: Keep 3072-number vectors and split each one across three database rows.
options.explanation: That fights the database instead of using the model's option to return shorter vectors.

options.text: Set `output_dimensionality` to 768; the model normalizes the shorter vectors.
options.explanation: Right. The docs recommend 768, 1536 or 3072, and say `gemini-embedding-2` normalizes vectors shorter than 3072 for you.

options.text: Switch back to `gemini-embedding-001`, because only it supports short vectors.
options.explanation: Both models support output sizes from 128 to 3072. With `gemini-embedding-001`, you would even have to normalize short vectors yourself.

options.text: Embed at 3072 and keep the first 1,024 numbers, with no further step.
options.explanation: Cutting vectors yourself needs a normalize step afterwards. Asking the API for a smaller size avoids the extra work.
